title: Two Shapes Make a New One

steps.body: Two matching triangle halves fit together to make a square. Trace the finished outside edge to name the new shape.
steps.narration: Two matching triangle halves fit together to make a square. Trace the finished outside edge to name the new shape.

widget.prompt: Two matching triangle halves of a square are joined along their long edges. Tap the shape they make.

hotspots.label: triangle
hotspots.feedback: Joining two matching triangle halves makes something larger with 4 sides, not another triangle.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: Straight-edged pieces cannot make a round shape.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: Close — but with equal edges joined, all four sides come out equal, making a square.

widget.missFeedback: Picture the matching long edges pressed together, then look at the outside.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — two matching triangle halves joined on their long edges make a square.

predict.prompt: Two shapes are joined along one edge. What happens to that shared edge?
predict.reveal: The shared edge is covered by the join, so it is no longer part of the new outline.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1s compose two.
invariants: A shape's defining attributes must stay fixed while colour, size and orientation vary.
misconceptions: Treating colour, size or orientation as if it decided what a shape is.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same shape?

widget.prompt: What new shape do two matching triangle halves make when joined?

options.label: A square
options.feedback: Correct — joining two matching triangle halves makes a square because their long edges match exactly.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Straight-sided pieces cannot join into a circle; every edge they contribute stays straight.

options.label: A cone
options.feedback: That is a solid, but joining flat pieces edge to edge keeps the result flat.

options.label: Nothing — shapes cannot be joined
options.feedback: Shapes combine readily; a new, larger shape is exactly what composing produces.

steps.body: The picture shows the two triangle pieces and the square they make. Their shared edge becomes an inside seam, not part of the square's outside edge.
steps.narration: The picture shows the two triangle pieces and the square they make. Their shared edge becomes an inside seam, not part of the square's outside edge.

widget.prompt: A square made from two matching triangle halves is opened along its diagonal seam. Tap one piece.

hotspots.label: square
hotspots.feedback: The square is the whole. Opening its diagonal seam reveals two triangle pieces.

hotspots.label: circle
hotspots.feedback: The straight diagonal seam cannot make a round piece. Each piece is a triangle.

hotspots.label: rectangle
hotspots.feedback: Each half has 3 sides after the diagonal seam opens, so each piece is a triangle.

widget.missFeedback: Follow the diagonal seam and count the 3 sides of one piece.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — opening the diagonal seam reveals two matching triangles.

widget.prompt: Two matching triangle halves of a square are joined along their long edges to make a square. How many corners does a square have?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the corners of both starting pieces; joining them hides the edges that meet inside.
That misses one corners of the finished square; count all the way around the outside.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Look again at the shape's sides and corners, counting each one exactly once.
